title: InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers
summary: InfuseLoop replaces the standard PLT loop recurrence, in which only the preceding in-trajectory hidden state crosses loop boundaries, with a cross-trajectory latent injection that aggregates causally available hidden states from later prediction trajectories via lightweight attention residuals. Costs are O(Rd) additional hidden-state storage, 0.3% decoding time over vanilla PLTs, and 23.3% over a non-looped baseline, while preserving token-parallel training and the vanilla PLT KV-cache footprint. It can fail if the reported stability and perplexity gains do not transfer beyond the paper's training scale, if looped-model decoding underutilizes the reader's single-GPU serving stack, or if integrating trajectory cross-dependencies complicates existing inference kernels.
rationale: The technique is a training-time architecture change to Parallel Looped Transformers, which the reader cannot train or adopt without foundation-model training infrastructure, though its efficiency profile merits monitoring.
technique: Cross-trajectory latent injection for looped transformers

It can fail if the reported stability and perplexity gains do not transfer beyond the paper's training scale, if looped-model decoding underutilizes the reader's single-GPU serving stack, or if integrating trajectory cross-dependencies complicates existing inference kernels.

At eight loops, reduces perplexity by 3.4–17.1% versus vanilla PLTs and 10.5–37.3% versus a non-looped baseline, with 0.84–1.99 points higher average downstream accuracy and only 0.3% decoding overhead versus vanilla PLTs.
